title: long-context-retrieval-sink-eval-notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for long-context and retrieval stress evaluations we will run during model onboarding for candidates with 8k/32k/128k context windows. Focus is on: (a) truncation behavior, (b) retrieval-induced context growth and stress, (c) attention-sink pathological patterns, and (d) regression detection heuristics tied to our eval harness.

Summary upfront (TL;DR):
- Small-scale runs (8k baseline) show ~95% question-answer retention for synthetic QA that uses earliest-window facts.
- At 32k, retention falls to ~88% when retrieval returns 4x extra documents per query and we force overlap/repetition.
- At 128k we observe two classes of failures: hard truncation of prompt leading to missing answer (30% of cases) and attention-sink slow degradation where model outputs hallucinations after a long repeated pattern (~22% of test set).
- Retrieval latency simulation (variable 50-500ms per doc) impacted decode throughput but not content correctness; the main driver of correctness regressions is total context length and repeated attention-heavy tokens.

Experiment design:
- Models: onboarding candidates (candidate-A v1.2, candidate-B v3.0-quant, baseline-redwood-v2).
- Context sizes tested: 8k, 32k, 128k (measured in tokens using our tokenizer; we generate both token- and char-based fixtures).
- Retrieval scenarios: (R0) oracle short (top-1), (R1) normal (top-5), (R2) noisy (top-20 with duplicates), (R3) pathological (top-50 with repeated paragraphs).
- Truncation modes: prefix-truncate (drop oldest), suffix-truncate (drop newest), chunked-window (sliding chunk with KV cache warmup), and pinned-template (pin system instruction + last 1k tokens).
- Attention-sink tests: create repeated arithmetic-like or GUID-like sequences designed to maximize attention matrix activity (e.g., 64k char-long repeated token patterns, nested lists).

Data and prompt sets (sketch):
- QA-anchor-early: 3k synthetic documents where the gold fact appears in doc #1 (earliest) and retrieval returns random permutations including later duplicates. Used to test truncation effects.
- Retrieval-noise: naturalistic customer docs (redacted) plus synthetic noise docs (3 variants) to emulate browser-like retrieval.
- LongSynth-sinks: synthetic patterns with repeated tokens and structured noise to stress attention.
- Prompt templates:
  * SYSTEM: "You are an assistant answering from context. If answer not in context reply: I-DONT-KNOW."
  * USER QA: "Given the following context, answer: [question]. Keep answer <= 50 tokens."
  * Retrieval injection: after 'CONTEXT START' we insert N docs separated by '---DOC---' markers so we can detect if splitting/truncation removes marker boundaries.

Metrics we collect (automated):
- QA Recall@1: exact/gold match after normalization.
- Token retention rate: fraction of gold-fact tokens still present in final context window at decode time.
- Truncation index: location (token offset) where truncation occurred relative to original context (prefix vs suffix).
- Hallucination rate: fraction of non-grounded assertions in answer (measured via script using gold facts + NER match heuristics).
- Attention concentration score: proxy computed from attention-weight distribution summaries (we log per-layer attention mass on repeated tokens).
- Latency/throughput: decode tokens/sec at different context sizes and retrieval delays.

Preliminary results (notes from runs):
- candidate-A v1.2 on 32k (R2 noisy): QA Recall 0.87, token retention 0.75, median truncation index ~ -6500 (we lost material near start of last retrieval batch).
- candidate-B v3.0-quant on 128k (R3 pathological): QA Recall 0.62, hallucination 0.22, attention-concentration spike in layers 7-9 correlated with hallucinations.
- baseline-redwood-v2 on 8k (R0 oracle): QA Recall 0.95, near-zero hallucination.

Representative failure cases (copied raw outputs):
1) Truncation mask problem, candidate-B: context ended abruptly at '...protocol 17.2' and answer referenced 'protocol 17.2', yet model replied 'I-DONT-KNOW' because system instruction got preserved but gold paragraph truncated.
2) Attention sink hallucination, candidate-B: after 40k tokens of repeating hex patterns, model began producing compound speculative statements unrelated to question.
3) Boundary marker loss: when docs are inserted with '---DOC---' markers we occasionally truncated inside markers -> merging paragraphs -> produced ambiguous context and wrong entity resolution.

Observations and hypotheses: 
- Repetition + scale (128k) triggers attention mass focusing on repeated tokens, reducing effective attention to factual tokens; this is consistent with our attention-concentration telemetry.
- Truncation policy choice (prefix vs suffix) matters: for retrieval-heavy workloads pinning system + recent context while dropping older retrievals yielded better QA recall in customer-simulated flows.
- Quantized model variants show increased hallucination under attention sink patterns, suggesting quantization noise interacts poorly with long-range dependencies.

Regression detection rules proposed for onboarding gate: 
- Primary gate: QA Recall@1 on QA-anchor-early >= baseline - 0.05 at each context length.
- Secondary gate: Hallucination rate delta <= +0.05 relative to baseline.
- Attention telemetry: if attention-concentration spike > 0.4 (normalized) and correlates with hallucination events > 10%, fail onboarding.
- Throughput/latency guardrail: decode tokens/sec should be within 30% of baseline for 8k workload and within 50% for 32k.

Repro checklist for each run: 
- Config saved: model hash, tokenizer hash, context-window param, truncation-mode, retrieval-scenario, seed.
- All raw contexts + prompts archived with deterministic filenames.
- Eval harness versioned (GH:inference-eval-suite tag).
- Telemetry: attention matrices (sampled layers), KV cache stats, and per-request truncated-index.

Immediate next steps / TODOs: 
- [ ] Expand LongSynth-sinks with more structured patterns (nested lists, deep recursion-like prompts).
- [ ] Add customer-derived retrieval traces to R2 and R3 buckets (coordinate with SE: Priya).
- [ ] Run complete onboarding matrix overnight for candidate-A, candidate-B, and candidate-C with all truncation modes.
- [ ] Implement automated alert when truncation-marker loss occurs (detect missing '---DOC---' markers).
- [ ] Write up short one-page summary for product-hosted-api to explain tradeoffs (prefix vs suffix) and recommended defaults.

Notes to self (informal):
- Consider instrumenting the retrieval layer to optionally compress/abstract repeated paragraphs (dedupe) before sending to model; might reduce attention sink issues.
- For pinned templates, test cost of reserving 1k tokens vs QA recall gain. Could be a small perf hit but big quality win.
- Flag: candidate-B v3.0-quant shows promising latency at 128k but quality regressions are concerning; probably fine-tune the quantization profile or try mixed precision for KV cache.

Raw commands (how I ran the harness locally):
- python run_eval.py --model candidate-B:v3.0-quant --context 128000 --retrieval-scenario R3 --truncation prefix --seed 42 --out runs/candidateB-128k-R3.jsonl
- quick inspect: jq '.results[] | select(.qa_recall < 1) | {id,qa_recall,trunc_index}' runs/candidateB-128k-R3.jsonl | head

Contact points: Priya Desai (retrieval traces), Evan Chen (telemetry ingestion), Liam O'Connor (quantization experiments).

If useful, next week I'll convert this into a short playbook with recommended default configs per workload (chatty app vs retrieval-heavy FAQ). For now keep this doc as the working source for notes and raw failure logs.

-- Asha
